name: The Barrens
summary: Across The Barrens, Horde outposts hold the roads while rival forces press in from every side. Once a forest before the Great Sundering, the central Kalimdor plain is now dry country of red dust, scrub, and wandering wildlife. The Crossroads anchors Horde traffic, but quilboar, centaur, and creeping corruption threaten its hold.

sections.title: Heart of the New Horde
sections.body: For generations, tauren nomads hunted kodo and zhevra across the plains and fought a repeating defensive war against Kolkar centaur. During the Third War, Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor and helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive back the centaur and cross the savanna into Mulgore. The Barrens now links Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale. The Crossroads and Camp Taurajo guard trade along the Gold Road, while orcish homesteads endure the harsh climate as they build a lasting home.

sections.title: A Land Under Siege
sections.body: Horde control of the savanna remains contested. Razormane quilboar, with their porcupine-like bristles, raid farms and supply lines from thorn-choked strongholds. Razorfen Kraul's dens loom to the south. On the eastern coast, Theramore forces hold Northwatch Hold, while dwarven prospectors dig into the titan complex of Bael Modan. Ratchet's goblins keep an uneasy neutrality in trade, welcoming travelers who bring coin.

sections.title: The Emerald Corruption
sections.body: Several oases break up the northern plains, their waters surging with unnatural vigor. The source lies in the Wailing Caverns, where the night elf druid Naralex tried to reach the Emerald Dream and restore the Barrens to its ancient forested state. A nightmare twisted his vision. Now corrupted water flows through the Forgotten Pools and Stagnant Oasis, giving rise to strange deviate plants, unnatural beasts, and the rogue Druids of the Fang.

faq.q: Why are there lush oases in the middle of a desert?
aliases: why is there water in barrens
faq.answer: The Forgotten Pools and Lushwater Oasis draw water from underground springs flowing out of the Wailing Caverns. The night elf druid Naralex tried to channel the springs through the Emerald Dream and green the dry land, but the effort went awry, filling the northern Barrens with potent, volatile natural magic.

The Horde garrisons the Crossroads, chiefly with orc and tauren warriors who serve Warchief Thrall. Its place where the main trade routes meet makes it the Horde's chief military and transit hub in central Kalimdor, linking Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale.

faq.q: Why are the quilboar attacking everyone?
faq.answer: The quilboar claim the Barrens as their ancestral birthright. They believe its great brambles grew from the blood of their demigod, Agamaggan, during the War of the Ancients. They see the arriving Horde and native tauren as trespassers taking their sacred foraging grounds and hunting territory.

faq.q: Why are Alliance soldiers in the Barrens?
faq.answer: The Alliance holds to the savanna's edges. Human troops from Theramore garrison Northwatch Hold to watch Horde movements, while dwarves at Bael Modan and Bael'dun Keep dig for ancient titan artifacts buried in the southern hills.

faq.q: Is Ratchet part of the Horde?
faq.answer: No. Ratchet is an independent goblin port run by Gazlowe. It welcomes Horde and Alliance travelers, smugglers, and adventurers for maritime trade, so long as they respect goblin commerce and keep weapons sheathed in town.

faq.q: What is going on with the silithid in the south?
faq.answer: Silithid, insect-like creatures, have emerged from earthen hives in the southern Barrens, especially around the Field of Giants. Their sudden arrival and fast-growing colonies threaten travelers and nearby outposts, and the Horde is investigating their origins.

angles.text: The Barrens is your realm's supply road. Holding the Crossroads and guarding convoys along the Gold Road help Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff endure.
Your nomadic ancestors roamed these savannas for generations before the orcs reached Kalimdor. They hunted sacred game and struggled to survive against the ruthless Kolkar centaur.
The altered waters from the Wailing Caverns mark a tragedy: Naralex's attempt to restore the Barrens fell to a nightmare.
These dry plains test your bond with the elements, from the spirits of the parched earth to the enchanted waters bubbling up in isolated oases.
